The SNPs an EHH plot had to choose between

Source: R/plot_ehh.R
ehh_candidates.Rd

plot_ehh() measures decay from a single focal SNP, and a gene usually holds many. It takes the one with the most balanced alleles and reports which – this returns the whole shortlist it chose from, chosen SNP first, so the decision is visible and can be overridden by passing a chr:pos back to focal.

Usage

ehh_candidates(
  x,
  focal,
  group = NULL,
  genes = NULL,
  min_haplotypes = 10,
  reference = DEFAULT_REFERENCE
)

Arguments

x

A parasite_haplotypes() object, or a PopStructure.

focal

As in plot_ehh(): a chr:pos id, a bare position, or a gene name in genes.

group

Optional metadata column, for the per-group columns.

genes

Gene table used to resolve focal (e.g. PF3D7_GENES).

min_haplotypes

Groups smaller than this are left out, as in plot_ehh().

reference

Reference id, used when focal names a whole chromosome.

Value

A tibble of snp_id, chr, pos, maf, n_hap and chosen, plus the per-group columns when group is given. The chosen SNP is the first row; the rest follow by descending maf.

Details

maf is the metric that decides it: minor-allele frequency across the haplotypes, which plot_ehh() maximises because EHH measured from a near-singleton is a flat line at 1 that says nothing about a sweep.

With group, each group gets a maf_<group> column and n_groups_variable counts the groups the SNP actually varies in. That is the other way a panel comes back empty: a SNP can be well balanced overall and monomorphic inside one group, which drops that group's curve with "the focal SNP is not variable in it". Sorting on n_groups_variable finds a SNP that works everywhere, when one exists.

See also

plot_ehh()

Examples

ps <- example_pop_structure(umap = FALSE)
hap <- parasite_haplotypes(ps, maf = 0.05)
ehh_candidates(hap, "pfcrt", genes = PF_EXAMPLE_DRUG_GENES)
